title: Zip Slip, archive parser differentials and zip-bomb defense
attackSurface: Entries inside an attacker-supplied ZIP archive inspected before extraction

references.note: Zip Slip archive extraction directory traversal in plexus-archiver

hostile.title: Zip Slip authorized_keys overwrite
hostile.why: CVE-2018-1002200 style archive entry that escapes the extraction root

hostile.title: Nested parent traversal
hostile.why: Traversal hidden behind a benign-looking first segment

hostile.title: Backslash traversal entry
hostile.why: Windows separator traversal in a cross-platform archive

hostile.title: Absolute POSIX entry
hostile.why: Absolute archive path replaces the extraction root

hostile.title: Windows drive entry
hostile.why: Drive-qualified archive entries can write outside the selected folder

hostile.title: UNIX symlink escape entry
hostile.why: A symlink entry can redirect later extraction writes outside the root

hostile.title: Duplicate path collision
hostile.why: Duplicate entries create extraction-order and overwrite ambiguity

hostile.title: Deflate ratio bomb
hostile.why: Highly compressible data crosses the bounded compression-ratio policy

benign.title: Nested documentation archive
benign.why: Directory plus nested document is a normal archive shape

benign.title: Deflated text file

entries.name: compressed.txt
entries.data: repeated text repeated text repeated text

benign.why: Normal deflate compression below security limits

benign.title: Empty archive
benign.why: A structurally valid empty ZIP is not hostile

benign.title: Well-known metadata
benign.why: Dotfile-style metadata paths are valid archive content

benign.title: Names near reserved words
benign.why: Names containing but not exactly matching prototype keys are benign

benign.title: Deep supported path
benign.why: Deep paths within the documented depth limit are valid
